messages.author: fc439899b88457c2
messages.subject: Interactive input of data
parts:
Hi,

I have a question, for which the answer is probably no, but I just want to make sure :) Is there a way to do interactive data input with shiny? Now you can change single values, but I need something more: directly editing a table, ie. change the values in a data.frame which stay changed. Alternatively I would like be able to move a line in a plot, which will result in changed data. 

The simple user case is prediction. Say estimate linear relationship between y and x. Then given the newdata I want to display the predictions based on it. The trick is that newdata provided is only one scenario. I would like for user of the app to change the scenarios of x to see how y changes. For that I need to interactively edit newdata. One way would be to edit the values of newdata directly, another would be to display the initial newdata on the graph and let the user change the graph. All the changes in the newdata would have to be reflected immediately in the prediction of y. This would be some kind of analytics dashboard. Is this at all possible?

Vaidotas Zemlys

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Interactive input of data
parts:
These kinds of components certainly could be written with Shiny but I don't believe anyone has done so yet. With Shiny, most things are possible, it's just a question of how much JavaScript you have to write (which you can then package up so any R users can take advantage of your work).

We do have a tableInput function in the shinyIncubator package that might help, it provides a 2D table editing widget. You can install the package like so:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio")
